case_sheet.raw_narrative: I booked return flight tickets from Delhi to Bengaluru for myself and my elderly mother on September 12, 2024 for travel on October 20, paying ₹19,800 via credit card (PNR: 6E-XK8912). On October 19, just 14 hours before scheduled departure, IndiGo sent an SMS stating the flight was cancelled due to 'operational and aircraft rotation constraints'. When I requested an immediate bank refund, IndiGo automatically transferred the ₹19,800 into an 'IndiGo Credit Shell' wallet account, valid only for 6 months. When I called their customer service helpline, they informed me that tickets booked under economy saver fare cannot be refunded to the bank account and credit shells cannot be converted to cash under any circumstances. I was forced to spend ₹34,000 on last-minute tickets on another carrier. I have the booking ticket, credit card deduction receipt, IndiGo cancellation SMS, and written chat logs with IndiGo customer care.

rights_explainer.standing_summary: You have a strong legal standing under Indian civil and consumer law. Under Airline Delays, Cancellations & Refund Withholding, withholding your legitimate funds of ₹19,800 or failing to deliver contracted quality is legally actionable. Indian law does not allow unilateral contract clauses or arbitrary forfeitures.
key_rights: **DGCA Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) (Section 3, Series M, Part IV)**: Refund must be made immediately if paid in cash, or within 7 days for credit/debit card transactions.

**DGCA Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) (Section 3, Series M, Part IV)**: Airlines cannot forcefully lock passenger money into an airline credit shell or travel voucher without explicit written passenger consent.
**Supreme Court of India Ruling (Pravasi Legal Cell & Ors. vs. Union of India (2020))**: Credit shell can only be an option, never a forced default.
**Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 2(11) & 35)**: Can be escalated to AirSewa grievance portal.

escalation_path.tier: Step 1: Formal Statutory Demand Notice (15-Day Cure Period)
escalation_path.action: Dispatch a formal legal notice via Registered Post AD / Speed Post and Email. Give them 15 working days to refund ₹19,800 plus interest.
escalation_path.why_it_works: Over 75% of Indian consumer & tenancy disputes settle at this stage once the opposite party sees precise statutory sections and realizes you are prepared to escalate.

escalation_path.tier: Step 2: National Consumer Helpline (NCH 1915) / Statutory Portal
escalation_path.action: File a grievance on consumerhelpline.gov.in (Toll-Free 1915) or AirSewa.
escalation_path.why_it_works: Government officers directly notify the nodal officer of the registered corporate entity, requiring a mandatory written status update within 30 days.

escalation_path.tier: Step 3: Online e-Daakhil / District Consumer Commission (DCDRC)
escalation_path.action: File an e-complaint on e-daakhil.nic.in before the District Consumer Forum. Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, claims up to ₹5 Lakh have ZERO court fees.
escalation_path.why_it_works: You do NOT need to hire an expensive advocate; consumers can represent themselves. The forum can award refund + 9-12% interest + compensation for mental harassment.
escalation_path.cost: ₹0 (for claims up to ₹5L), ₹200 for claims up to ₹10L

rights_explainer.realistic_timeline: 15 days for initial notice response; 30 to 45 days if escalated via NCH; 3 to 6 months for formal Consumer Commission order.
rights_explainer.financial_outlook: Eligible to claim full ₹19,800 + 9-12% annual interest + ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 for mental agony & litigation costs.

================================================================================
FORMAL LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE (WITHOUT PREJUDICE)
DISPATCHED VIA: REGISTERED POST WITH A.D. / SPEED POST & OFFICIAL EMAIL
================================================================================

DATE: 08 November, 2026

TO:
InterGlobe Aviation Ltd. (IndiGo Airlines)
[Full Registered Address / Corporate Office / Residential Address]
Email: [Official Email / Nodal Grievance Officer]

FROM:
[Complainant / Aggrieved Citizen Name]
[Residential Address / Contact Phone / Email]

SUBJECT:
DEMAND NOTICE FOR IMMEDIATE REFUND OF INR 19,800/- WITH ACCRUED INTEREST
AND COMPENSATION FOR DEFICIENCY IN SERVICE, WRONGFUL RETENTION, AND UNFAIR TRADE PRACTICE.

SIR / MADAM,

Under explicit instructions and on behalf of my client / self, the present Legal Notice is hereby served upon you:

1. FACTUAL BACKGROUND & TRANSACTION DETAILS:
   a) That the Claimant entered into a valid and lawful commercial/tenancy/service transaction with you, wherein full payment/deposit of INR 19,800/- was duly remitted.
   b) I booked return flight tickets from Delhi to Bengaluru for myself and my elderly mother on September 12, 2024 for travel on October 20, paying ₹19,800 via credit card (PNR: 6E-XK8912)
   c) That despite multiple written communications, emails, and follow-ups, you have wilfully failed, neglected, and refused to remediate the defect / return the legitimate funds due to the Claimant.

2. STATUTORY VIOLATIONS & LEGAL GROUNDS:
   Under the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR), Section 3, Series M, Part IV, and the landmark Supreme Court ruling in Pravasi Legal Cell vs. Union of India (2020), an airline is statutorily mandated to refund cancelled flights directly into the original mode of payment. Forcing a credit shell or travel voucher without explicit consent constitutes a direct Deficiency in Service under Section 2(11) and an Unfair Trade Practice under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

3. WRONGFUL RETENTION & DAMAGES:
   By virtue of your arbitrary conduct, the Claimant has suffered severe financial distress, inconvenience, and mental agony. You have illegally retained money that does not belong to you, depriving the Claimant of its rightful use.

4. REQUISITE DEMANDS & 15-DAY CURE NOTICE:
   You are hereby formally called upon to:
   i. Immediately refund the principal amount of INR 19,800/- (Indian Rupees 19,800 only) into the Claimant's designated bank account within 15 (FIFTEEN) DAYS of the receipt of this Notice;
   ii. Pay interest calculated at the rate of 12% per annum from the date the amount fell due until the date of actual payment;
   iii. Pay an amount of INR 15,000/- towards damages for mental harassment and costs incurred in issuing this formal notice.

TAKE NOTICE that if you fail to comply with the legitimate demands set forth above within the stipulated period of 15 days, the Claimant shall be constrained to institute appropriate legal proceedings against you, including filing a formal Consumer Complaint under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 before the Competent District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission / Civil Court of competent jurisdiction, entirely at your sole risk, cost, and consequences.

A copy of this Legal Notice is retained in records for future legal proceedings.

Yours faithfully,

_____________________________
[Complainant / Authorized Signatory]
Enclosures:
1. Proof of Payment / Bank Statement
2. Written Agreement / Booking Confirmation
3. Relevant WhatsApp / Email Communication Records
================================================================================

Please initiate the bank refund within 7 working days, failing which this will be filed with AirSewa and the District Consumer Commission.

statutory_references.summary: When a flight is cancelled or delayed beyond specified thresholds by the airline, passenger has the absolute choice between alternate flight or immediate full refund.
